title: Lay a corduroy log mat across a bog and push the rover over it
instruction: The track ahead is a bog. Lay the logs, then push the rover across onto the far bank.
context: Trail crews cross soft ground with a corduroy mat: logs laid crosswise, tight between the banks, so that none can roll or drop away under a wheel. Here four logs must be laid that way and proved by pushing a free-rolling rover over them; a wheel that reaches the bog fouls the trial. Unlike TK-UYFM6W (two flat runners into fixed seats across a dock gap), the mat has no seats: four loose logs must fill the gap side by side, each crosswise and seated on the mud, and the rover is pushed over them on free wheels, so a log missing, askew or riding up puts a wheel in the bog.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Track: two fixed plywood decks, 2.0 cm tall and 24 cm wide (y -12 to 12), clamped to the table, tops painted earth brown: the near deck from x 6 to 37, the far deck from x 45.3 to 74. Bog: the 8.3 cm gap between them, a sheet of dark brown rubber 0.8 mm thick on the table (x 37 to 45.3, y -12 to 12). Verges: two mats of artificial turf 0.4 mm thick, 30 x 14 cm, on the table beside the track (centred at x 33, y 19 and y -19). Rover: a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M with the Bronco body shell, decals removed, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, 0.51 kg, tyres 5.6 cm across, motor pinion removed so its wheels roll freely, on the near deck facing the bog, the midpoint between its axles at (23.5, 0), its front bumper 4 mm short of the bog. Logs: four logs of a dense hardwood (jatoba, about 900 kg/m3), 18 cm long with a six-sided section (2.0 cm across the corners, 1.7 cm across the flats; hexagonal dowel, or a round dowel planed with flats), 42 g each, natural brown, lying along x on the verges at (31, 20), (37, 20), (31, -20) and (37, -20).
scoring: 0 if at any time a tyre touches the bog (its lowest point within 4 mm of the bog sheet's top, over the bog); a tyre is over the bog with no log under it (no log lying crosswise in the bog within 1.6 cm of the tyre's lowest point along the track, under it across the track, with the tyre within 4 mm of the log's top, the log lying in the bog and not held up); a tyre is over the bog before all four logs are laid as for the 0.5 credit below; a tyre leaves the track (its lowest point outside the decks and the bog seen from above: the rover may not go round); the rover moves faster than 0.3 m/s (it could jump the bog between control steps); or all four tyres are more than 8 mm above the surfaces under them (deck tops, the top of a log lying in the bog over the bog, the table elsewhere): the rover lifted. Otherwise, at the end, with the rover and the logs at rest (each moving under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s for the last 20 control steps, 1 s at 20 Hz) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and no point along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover or a log): 0.5 if all four logs lie in the bog crosswise (within 10 degrees of the track's width and of level), resting on the bog (centre no more than 1.4 cm above the table), each spanning both wheel paths, with no gap wider than 5 mm between neighbouring logs or at the decks (taken corner to corner, 2.0 cm per log; the bog leaves 3 mm of play for four logs, so the gap test catches a log missing, askew or riding up); 1.0 if, in addition, all four tyres rest on the far deck; otherwise 0. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Roll the rover back to its mark on the near deck and lay the four logs back on the verges at their marks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The bog is a rigid sheet: a wheel does not sink, it fouls the trial when it reaches the bog (judged from tyre height). The rover base is rigid at the crawler's published size and mass; wheels roll freely with 0.006 N m s/rad drag; suspension rigid. Logs are six-sided (friction 0.9, angular damping 4.0, heavy) standing in for rough bark, since a perfect cylinder rolls away in simulation. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms reached over the logs and then drew back; no log was moved and the rover stayed put); demo: 1.0
